newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BCE MILLING WHEAT PRICES PAUSE FOR BREATH.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BCE MILLING WHEAT PRICES PAUSE FOR BREATH.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) paused for breath on Wednesday but traders said quality worries still prevailed.
"The market has its reservations about the Agriculture Ministry's wheat quality assessment," said Robert Vajo of Termin grains trading company.

The Agriculture Ministry said earlier on Wednesday that about 45 percent of this year's five million tonnes wheat crop would be above euro or (domestic) B1 standard, a result better than sources outside the ministry had suggested.
Milling wheat futures rose by between 40 to 200 forints per tonne for four maturities, eased marginally for another two and were unchanged for the three most distant maturities.
Milling wheat prices ended at 28,310 forints for September, 30,880 for December and 33,630 for May.
Total BCE grains turnover, half of which was made up of milling wheat for most of the last month, remained minimal due to the few milling wheat contracts today.
Total turnover dropped to 447 lots or 221 million forints from Tuesday's mediocre 1,334 lots or 766.8 million forints.
Maize, which finished higher for four maturities, accounted for 230 lots of Wednesday's turnover.
Vajo said expectations of a good domestic maize crop (of above six million tonnes) remained but prices were pushed up by international prices.
He added that Hungary was likely to have export opportunities in the Czech Republic, Poland, Slovenia and possibly Belarus but neither quantities nor prices could be estimated at the moment.
Maize futures prices for this year's crop finished between 18,100 forints for September and 21,600 for July while 1998 crop prices ended at 24,080 forints for October and 24,100 for November.
